messages:
tim_sales: Heads up - Initech POC blocked. App tier > private endpoint connections intermittently fail with TLS alerts and 502s. Works from dev-box but not app subnet. They turned on perimeter TLS inspection + strict egress rules recently.

sam_se: Can you share minimal logs and DNS resolution from the affected host? Typical suspects: split-horizon DNS resolving to wrong ENI, firewall doing MITM and presenting non-trusted CA, or NAT hairpin issues.

tim_sales: They sent this curl output (IPs redacted):
```
$ curl -v https://svc.initech.corp/ -o /dev/null
* Connected to 10.50.7.9 (10.50.7.9) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, unknown ca
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL connect error
```

julia_neteng: Ran dig via their app host: returns 10.50.7.9 (private ENI). tcpdump on our endpoint shows ClientHello SNI=svc.initech.corp sometimes and SNI=corp-proxy.initech.com other times. Looks like their inspector rewrites SNI intermittently (round-robin across inspection nodes).

sam_se: Intermittent SNI rewrite explains flakiness. Also ask them to check if their inspection device re-signs the cert with their internal CA. If so, app hosts need that CA in trust store or bypass must be applied.

ori_oncall: Also check if OCSP stapling is required; blocked egress to OCSP responder can cause failures. Run `openssl s_client -connect 10.50.7.9:443 -servername svc.initech.corp -status` and `curl -I https://ocsp.example-ca.net/` from app host.

tim_sales: Sent commands. Their reply: OCSP reachable. Vendor confirms the appliance re-signs certs for inspection and rewrites SNI unless an explicit bypass for the destination FQDN/CIDR is configured. They prefer not to install their CA in prod app images.

sam_se: Recommend 1) Add bypass rule for Private endpoint CIDR for the POC (fast). 2) Or run app traffic via a dedicated proxy/bastion that bypasses inspection. 3) Long-term: private endpoint mTLS or a dedicated Dedicated deployment behind customer perimeter.

julia_neteng: Quick operational test they can try: from app host `curl --resolve svc.initech.corp:443:10.50.7.9 https://svc.initech.corp/` to bypass DNS and see if SNI still gets rewritten. If tcpdump on endpoint shows changed SNI, bypass needed.

tim_sales: Customer will try bypass rule change; asked if we can relax server SNI validation as a temporary POC patch.

sam_se: We can add an opt-in SNI-accept-list but it's ~2 dev-days + config approval; security tradeoffs documented. Not recommended unless they can't change their firewall rules.

infra-bot: Task created: POC-1999990000 Investigate intermittent SNI rewrite for Initech POC. Assignee: sam_se. ETA: 48h.

tim_sales: They implemented bypass at 16:20 and reported successful 200s from app hosts. Keeping watch until customer sign-off. Thanks team.
